page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 6 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores running at 2.5 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, fall into the bottom 25% tier, with single-threaded gzip compression registering in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core, Passmark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, consistently achieve mid-range, average performance. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads and writes also align with average tier expectations, though the overall Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%.

The instance is suitable for workloads that benefit from multi-threaded processing and a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, such as static web serving, Redis database operations, and software compilation. However, its weak single-core performance makes it less optimal for single-threaded execution or latency-sensitive sequential tasks. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated Intel Xeon architecture offers predictable multi-threaded compute density for general-purpose workloads without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware.
